title: Onboard Quant Regression Playbook: Slice Deltas and Triage
content:
Purpose and audience:
This is a tactical playbook for applied-ML engineers and onboarding owners to triage, prioritize, and act on quality deltas observed when moving new model variants into serving with integer/low-bit quantization (int8, int4, AWQ, GPTQ). Intended for eng-applied-ml, solutions engineering, and platform owners who run model rollouts and maintain promptset health.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
Across the candidate models we onboarded in Feb 2025, the dominant regression modes for AWQ and GPTQ int4 variants were distributional hallucination in open-ended instruction prompts, tokenization-sensitive cutoffs in code-completion slices, and precision loss on numerics for short-answer QA. Int8 variants showed fewer severe regressions but higher variance on long-context summarization slices. This playbook defines an evaluation rubric, triage flow, and recommended mitigations mapped to severity tiers and rollout actions.

Evaluation rubric (what we measure and why):
- Slice-level metrics (primary): delta-ROUGE, delta-BLEU (where applicable), delta-ExactMatch (short QA), and human-rated severity score (0–3).
- Behavioral checks: safety classification divergence, hallucination triggers (entity hallucination rate), and instruction-following dropout (missing required steps).
- Cost/latency: tokens/sec delta and memory footprint (to ensure quant benefits aren’t outweighed by regressions).
- Stability: variance across seeds and temperature settings.

Prompt set construction notes:
- We keep three canonical prompt groups per product vertical: instruction dialogs, code-edit/completion, and short-fact QA. Each contains 200+ exemplars drawn from production telemetry (anonymized), synthetic edgecases, and curated adversarial seeds.
- Slice definitions are intentionally orthogonal: prompt intent, token-length quintiles, presence-of-numeric-answers, and tokenizer-boundary sensitivity.
- We tag prompts with provenance: prod-telemetry/V1, synthetic/edge1, internal-eval/seedX. This helps prioritize regressions that hit high-frequency production signals.

Observed slice-level deltas (high-level):
- Instruction-dialog (long-turn, multi-step): AWQ-int4 shows a median -0.18 ROUGE and human severity 2 in 12% of prompts; hallucinations often appear when the prompt requires referencing a multi-step history.
- Code completion (short to medium): GPTQ-int4 produced truncated outputs (tokenization boundary failures) in 7% of examples; int8 variants had 2% failure with less severe correctness loss.
- Short-answer factual QA (numbers/dates): Both AWQ/GPTQ-int4 showed spikes in answer digit corruption (e.g., swapping year digits) around 3–5% of prompts; human severity labeled these as 2 for business-critical slices.
- Summarization long-context (>= 2048 tokens): int8 variants had increased variance in ROUGE (-0.05 median but tail -0.22) suggesting occasional decoding instability under memory pressure.

Triage flow (stepwise):
1) Automated triage job runs nightly and emits candidate regressions with: slice, prompt id, metric delta, inference config, and seed.
2) Triage owner (onboarding engineer) inspects top N by weighted impact score (freq * severity).
3) Quick checks (automated): rerun with same quant seed, vary temperature/decoding, and compare with FP32 and an alternate quant backend. If delta disappears, mark as transient and annotate.
4) If persistent, run human review on 20-shot sample of the prompt slice, capture qualitative notes and label error mode: hallucination, truncation, numeric-flip, style-change, hallucinated-entity.
5) Map to action bucket (see next section).

Action buckets and decision matrix:
- Block rollout: major correctness regressions on production-high-frequency slices (severity 3, impact score > threshold). Action: rollback to previous variant, open incident, prioritize mitigation sprint.
- Canary with guardrails: moderate regressions (severity 2) on medium-impact slices. Action: 10% canary with strict routing (dedicated capacity, lower concurrency), add prompt-level fallbacks to FP32 for flagged prompts.
- Promote with mitigation: small regressions (severity 1) that are recoverable via prompt engineering or caching. Action: promote but instrument per-prompt fallback and add promptset-specific post-processing (e.g., numeric regex correction).
- Accept: negligible deltas (severity 0) and clear cost gains.

Common root causes and suggested targeted mitigations:
- Tokenizer-boundary truncation (GPTQ-int4): short-term fix: post-decode whitespace/token smoothing and n-gram join heuristics. Long-term: re-evaluate tokenizer vocab mapping in quantized model and add few-shot calibration focusing on boundary examples.
- Numeric corruption: add numeric normalization and constrained decoding; optionally run a lightweight verifier model (FP32) for numeric-only outputs and overwrite if mismatch.
- Long-history hallucination: enable prefix KV caching in dedicated-serving paths to preserve context fidelity; increase MLP numeric precision in critical layers (mixed-precision hack).
- Summarization instability under memory pressure: prefer int8 for long-context workloads or increase batch fragmentation thresholds to reduce per-request peak memory.

Recommended experiments to prioritize (short backlog):
- AWQ-int4 + softplus-calibration: small calibration dataset (1k prompts) focused on numeric and multi-step instruction prompts. Measure delta in human severity.
- Tokenizer re-map probe for truncated code completions: generate tokenization overlap table for top-200 code prompts and try alternative BPE splits.
- FP32 hybrid fallback policy: implement prompt classifier that routes a small fraction (by slice) to FP32 to measure cost-performance tradeoff in production.

Human-eval protocol (practical notes):
- Labeling instructions: show the FP32 golden, quantized output, and the prompt. Ask raters to annotate: correctness (0/1/2), hallucination flags (entities, dates, numeric anomalies), and suggested severity.
- Inter-rater agreement target: Krippendorff alpha >= 0.6 for correctness on critical slices. If lower, refine rubric.
- Sampling: stratified by prompt provenance and production frequency; oversample synthetic edgecases 2x during initial triage.

Rollout checklist (pre-canary):
- Automated tests: all regression slices pass delta thresholds on nightly bench.
- Guardrails: downstream route rules for fallback and rate-limits for FP32 fallback calls.
- Observability: create per-model per-slice dashboards with alert thresholds (human-severity rolling mean > 1.2).
- Playbook attachment: link to this document from the rollout PR and include mitigation owner assignment.

Notes on metrics and thresholds (empirically tuned):
- Critical threshold: any slice with production-frequency > 0.1% of requests and delta-ExactMatch > 0.03 => block.
- Canary threshold: weighted impact score > 0.001 and human-severity median >= 1 => require 10% canary with alert.
- Stability threshold: variance multiplier (quantized/FP32) > 2x across seeds => require further probing.

Case study (recent onboarding example):
- Model: meta-open-13b-v2 (FP32 baseline) -> AWQ-int4 variant
- Issue: numeric-flip in invoice-extraction short-answer slice (prod-frequency 0.02%).
- Triage: rerun deterministic seed -> persistent. Human eval (n=30) found 7/30 incorrect numeric totals.
- Root cause: quantized linear layer overflow on small-scale numeric embeddings.
- Actions: blocked rollout, added mixed-precision patch to numeric-projection layers (+1.2% memory), reran eval -> numeric errors reduced to 0/30. Promoted after 2-day canary.

Open questions and research items:
- How effective are tiny calibration datasets vs layer-wise mixed-precision patches across architectures? (priority: medium)
- Can we build an automated numeric verifier that is cheap enough to run as a post-process at scale? (priority: high)
- Should we maintain a small FP32 shadow fleet for only the top 20 slices that are most business-critical? (priority: operational cost study)

Appendix: quick checklist for a new model-onboard run
- Prepare promptset with tags and production-frequency annotations.
- Run nightly quant-eval for AWQ, GPTQ, int8 variants with 3 seeds each.
- Auto-triage top N (default N=150) by weighted impact.
- Human-review stratified sample of flagged slices.
- Map to action bucket and ensure mitigation owner assigned.
- Attach canary config and guardrail PR before promote.
